title: Broader current consumer and writer-readiness reconciliation
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan reconciliation
scope: Reconcile current LibreCAD 3 DWG read-only consumer policy with library writer experiments
Separate the documented stock-FreeCAD converter/importer route from ACIS-capable add-on/kernel routes
Refresh ACadSharp and LibreDWG ACIS/AcDs writer evidence and preserve exact revision boundaries
Refine the existing composed qualification sequence without increasing per-slice validation cost

method.kind: Read current project documentation, release/issue/PR pages, then reconcile evidence stages with the local implementation plan
method.limitations: Findings are documentation, issue, and PR observations only. ACadSharp issue results are reporter-scoped and release-specific; its writer PRs are unmerged. LibreDWG issue #1411 describes a specific build and was not rerun. No source checkout, executable, peer artifact, native application, or drawing was used.

sources.revision: master documentation page accessed 2026-10-18; page describes a pinned libdxfrw revision
sources.observed: The project declares DWG import read-only, behind WITH_DWG_IMPORT and disabled by default; DWG writing is not implemented, exposed, or planned absent all stated gates. It reports 15 read-direction claims at its pinned library revision (11 EXPERIMENTAL and 4 PENDING_NATIVE), none promoted, and a frozen claim set. This is a downstream policy snapshot, not a runtime result for this checkout.

The documented stock DXF importer cannot read embedded ACIS solids, and the documented DWG workflow uses an external converter to DXF followed by a selected FreeCAD DXF importer. Documentation does not establish behavior for the exact platform/build profile in the local plan.

Issue #1195 reports silent omission of modeler entities from DXF output, including block-contained solids. Linked PR #1240 proposes ACIS entity and ModelerGeometry writer work but remains an unmerged branch with no review or deployment shown and depends on open ACDS schema refactor #1174. This is not released-writer qualification or evidence of a libdxfrw defect.

A user reports that a no-op AC1032 roundtrip using ACadSharp 3.7.16 caused AutoCAD LT 2026 audit/recovery to discard standalone MLeader context objects; the report describes two fixes that repaired the tested drawings but provides no public sample. It is a version- and family-scoped report, not independently reproduced here.

sources.revision: mutable master documentation and issue #1411 for LibreDWG 0.14.8593 / commit prefix 8a1ae764; pages accessed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Project history says the R2013+ Prototype1b/AcDs path is not fully implemented and describes brute-force SAB extraction. Issue #1411 reports loss of a locally authored SAB carrier after conversion on its pinned 0.14.8593 build. The mutable documentation and issue report are separate evidence snapshots; this review did not rerun either route.

cq-acis documents an experimental bounded SAT/SAB/ASM parser/converter for selected geometry using CadQuery/OCCT; it does not parse DWG/DXF outer ownership and shares OCCT kernel lineage with FreeCAD. ezdxf exposes raw SAT/SAB browsing and limited projection, but its drawing add-on does not render ACIS and is not a B-rep kernel.

assessment.planImpact: Refines the existing consumer and writer readiness gates: preserve LibreCAD 3's read-only DWG product policy independently from experimental library writer paths; qualify stock FreeCAD only for its named converter/importer and supported entities; keep ACIS parser, shared OCCT kernel, AcDs owner/key linkage, semantic body validity, and native writer acceptance as separate results. Peer failures and open branches inform test design but do not become local findings or per-slice dependencies.

implementationReadyChecks: Do not expose or imply LibreCAD 3 DWG writing unless its consumer policy and all published gates change independently of library writer experiments.
Record stock-FreeCAD converter, selected DXF importer, OS/build, per-entity disposition, unsupported count, and warnings as one named consumer route; do not use it to qualify ACIS semantics.
For any writer route, require per-object disposition, owner/reference closure, strict independent readback, and native audit/open at a composed gate; same-library reread alone is insufficient.
Keep optional peer runs outside the fast per-slice loop and pin released artifacts; label open-branch tests as experiments, not support evidence.
For ACIS/AcDs, report carrier extraction and byte identity, owner/key linkage, parser completeness/losses, kernel validity/closure, analytic metrics, and consumer acceptance separately.
Keep unknown or unsupported data visible through explicit diagnostics or fail closed before publishing output; do not silently omit modeler geometry or its containing block contents.
